Caroline Beer's analysis of 22 November 2024 for the LSE USAPP found that Mexico's progressive LGBTQ+ legislation is rarely enforced fairly or uniformly, that rights exist formally but are rarely enjoyed in practice, and cautioned explicitly that her earlier work must not be read as evidence that LGBTQ+ people are safe from state or private violence including murder and torture.

manifest.quote: Mexico City's law of 21 December 2009 took effect on 4 March 2010 and was upheld 9-2 by the Supreme Court on 5 August 2010

The constitutional anti-discrimination framework was tightened on 10 June 2011, when Article 1 was amended to prohibit discrimination motivated by gender, sexual preferences or any other ground attacking human dignity, following a federal anti-discrimination law of 29 April 2003 and the insertion of the precise term sexual orientation into Article 1.

Same-sex marriage is legal nationwide: Mexico City's law of 21 December 2009 took effect on 4 March 2010 and was upheld 9-2 by the Supreme Court on 5 August 2010, and by 31 December 2022 every state had legalized same-sex marriage by legislation, executive order or judicial ruling, though only twenty allowed adoption.
